sampling.calmNegativeDownsampling: NONE — every eligible frame is kept
sampling.note: the train path keeps all negatives within 120 s of an onset and 25 % of calm stretches, then train.ts undoes it with 1/keepProbability weights. This corpus needs no such correction: metrics computed on it are already at natural prevalence.

power.note: projection only — SE scales as 1/√(independent clusters) and sessions are the cluster. The MEASURED paired session-clustered bootstrap SE is produced by `npm run forecast:eval` and written to src/shared/forecast/eval-report.json (field `power.measuredPairedSe`).

power.question: is a ~0.01 lead-censored AUC difference decidable on this corpus? The 48-session split could not decide 0.006, which is why 'the neural net did not win' was a shrug.
power.metric: lead-censored ROC-AUC (onset ≥ 20 s away vs calm), paired, clustered by session

bootstrap.estimatorCheck: weighted rank-sum verified against lib.rocAuc at unit weights for all 3 models (|Δ| < 1e-12)

reference.source: scripts/forecast/adjudicate.ts over the 48-session eval split (GAUNTLET round 8)

power.whyTheCorpusWasGrown: the first eval set was 48 sessions / 78 onsets / 858 lead-censored positives. Its paired SE was ≈0.009 while every margin the five-family bake-off produced was 0.001–0.006, so round 8 could not tell a 190-parameter GLM from a 14 803-parameter CNN and said so. Resolving a +0.006 gap needed ~7-8× the sessions; this corpus is 18.75×, and the comparison it could not decide is now decided (GAUNTLET round 10).
power.caveatSameGenerator: this corpus is FRESH SAMPLING from the same simulator, not new recorded data. It removes sampling noise; it does not remove simulator misspecification. Any bias the training and hold-out corpora share is invisible to it, and the round-8 open question — that the raw 1 Hz stream carries signal the 18 window aggregates destroy — still needs a real corpus.
power.caveat: this SE is measured on the shipped head vs the gate baseline. The bake-off contenders themselves are NOT re-scored here — their scripts are frozen and their scores exist only for the 48-session split — but the SE of a paired lead-AUC difference is a property of the corpus, the metric and the clustering far more than of which two similar-strength models are differenced, so it is the right yardstick for planning the re-run. Re-running the five contenders against `--data data/forecast/holdout/holdout-dataset.jsonl` is what actually settles the bake-off.

gate.metric: lead-censored ROC-AUC (onset ≥ 20 s away vs calm)
gate.baselineRationale: the strongest 24-feature multivariate logistic regression on the SAME feature basis the shipped head sees — the model a judge means by 'did you try logistic regression?'. The shipped head must not lose to it, and growing the feature set moves the bar with it.
gate.marginRequiredRationale: zero by design. The bar is 'a logistic regression on the same features must not beat the shipped head', and it fails the build the moment one does. Round 8 additionally could not have demanded more — on 48 eval sessions the paired SE was ≈0.009 and no positive margin was measurable. That constraint is gone: `marginCi95` below is the measured interval on this corpus. The bar stays at zero because a gate should encode the promise, not the current comfortable distance from it.

marginCi95.note: paired session-clustered bootstrap of (shipped − gate baseline) on lead-censored ROC-AUC, same resamples for both models. `resolved` means the interval excludes 0.

context.note: the pre-bake-off gate: +0.03 over the best SINGLE-feature logistic. Reported so the two bars can be compared — the 18→12→1 MLP that shipped before this swap passed THIS one by +0.1514 while losing to the full logistic by −0.0077.
context.plainLogisticLevelBlockNote: the plain logistic on the round-8 basis (18 level features). Context for what the trend block buys a plain additive model; the gate anchors to the full 24-feature fit so growing the feature set moves the bar with it.

rules.prearm: recallAt30 — a pre-arm was ACTIVE at onset (the reducer's own forecast_hit receipt) or fired within the prior 30 s. The strict product rule: the fuse was actually shortened.
rules.nudge: recallAt30Nudge — ANY nudge-or-higher alarm inside (onset − 30 s, onset]. The rule the five-family bake-off compared every contender on: the student got some warning.

operatingPointSelection.rule: TWO STAGES, because the product makes two promises with two budgets. Stage 1 picks the NUDGE line at the frozen pre-arm reference: max recall@30s under the nudge rule (a forecast_nudge or forecast_prearm event inside (onset−30s, onset]) subject to the alarm-load ceiling — round 8's rule, unchanged. Stage 2 then picks the PRE-ARM line at that nudge threshold: max recall@30s under the pre-arm rule (a pre-arm active at onset or fired in the prior 30s — the fuse was actually shortened) subject to the design's < 2 false pre-arms/hour and the same alarm-load ceiling. research_churn frame FPR ≤ ceiling throughout. Ties go to the quieter threshold. A SINGLE joint objective on nudge recall was tried first and is wrong: raising the pre-arm line deletes pre-arm events, which buys alarm-load headroom, which buys a lower nudge threshold — so it selects the worst pre-arm line on the grid (0.90, pre-arm recall 0.116) to win +0.07 of nudge recall.
operatingPointSelection.bothAxes: BOTH the nudge and the pre-arm threshold are searched. The inherited 0.80 pre-arm line was derived for the previous GLM's risk scale; a threshold is a cut on a scale, and round 10 measured every non-linear contender losing pre-arm recall at 0.80 for that reason alone. Re-deriving it is the condition the round-10 recommendation made non-negotiable before this swap.
operatingPointSelection.selectedOn: 3-fold cross-fitted TRAIN sessions — a fold-f session is scored by member f (the only member whose fit set excluded it), rescaled to the shipped blend's calibration-slice logit spread and read through the SHIPPED Platt; a calibration-slice session is scored by the shipped net, which never trained on it. No eval row is read here; no cross-fit model ships.

ceilings.loadMetric: NUDGES per hour — the toast rate, exactly as round 8 defined it. Not nudges + pre-arms: a pre-arm has its own stated budget (< 2 false pre-arms/hour) and putting it under the nudge ratio as well double-counts it. Measured and tried: because RAISING the pre-arm line deletes pre-arm events, a joint ceiling hands the search free headroom to lower the nudge line and therefore selects the WORST pre-arm threshold on the grid. alarmsPerHour is still reported on every row.
ceilings.stage2FloorRationale: one standard error of a recall estimate on this search corpus, sqrt(p(1-p)/onsets). An over-eager pre-arm consumes an escalation — the reducer latches the band, suppresses nudges, and a stand-down before the onset spends the warning for nothing — so the pre-arm axis is not allowed to measurably degrade the primary promise.

ifElseHeuristic.note: 3-rule strawman: fast switching OR grey dwell OR low desk presence

bestSingleFeatureLogistic.note: CONTEXT ONLY — the pre-bake-off gate baseline. One input; the shipped model beating it by a wide margin proves nothing, which is why the gate no longer uses it.

fullLogistic.fit: class-weighted full-batch GD (lib.trainLogistic, 250 epochs) — the historical baseline

fullLogisticConverged.fit: the same 24 features, L-BFGS to convergence on ALL train rows, importance-weighted to natural prevalence, at the λ train.ts selected on its train-internal val split (never on eval) — the honest ceiling of the plain additive logistic, and given MORE data than the shipped model

plainLogisticLevelBlock.note: CONTEXT ONLY — the plain logistic on the round-8 feature basis (the level block, before the trend features were appended). Its distance from `fullLogistic` is what the six trend features buy a plain additive model on this corpus.

fullLogisticStrongest.note: GATE BASELINE — the strongest 24-feature multivariate logistic we can produce

current.note: THE CONTEST THAT CHOSE THE SHIPPED HEAD. 17 fits — 8 families at BOTH feature bases — refit on split:"train" rows only and scored on this same 900-session corpus, with a paired session-clustered bootstrap and the feature-vs-architecture decomposition. Every loser is in it on purpose.

historical.note: HISTORICAL. Round 8's five-family contest on the 48-session eval SPLIT and the feature basis of 2026-09-12, which recorded "lr18+pairwise" as SHIPPED. That result has since been superseded twice: the basis grew (round 9) and the contest was re-run with enough power to decide it (round 10), where the head it chose FAILED this report's own gate. It is kept because the retraction is only legible next to it.

bakeOffPower.description: THE CONTEST THAT CHOSE THE SHIPPED HEAD. Eight model families fitted at BOTH feature bases (the 18 level features of round 8 and the 24 that ship today) — 17 fits in total — every one refit on split:"train" rows of data/forecast/dataset.jsonl and scored on the same 900-session / 1 230-onset hold-out corpus the committed eval-report.json uses, through one replay, one metric, one operating point and one escalation reducer. Every loser is here on purpose: publishing what lost is the only thing that makes the winner's margin mean anything. NON-GATING.
bakeOffPower.whyThisExists: round 8 ran the same contest on 48 held-out sessions, where the paired session-clustered SE of a model-vs-model lead-AUC difference was ≈ 0.009 and every margin on offer was 0.4–0.7 of one SE. It shipped the simplest model and said, honestly, that it could not tell the field apart. That was an underpowered shrug, not a measurement. This corpus is 18.75× the sessions; the measured SE is ≈ 0.003; and the comparison resolves — the other way.

protocol.calibration: every model is Platt-calibrated with the SHIPPED robust calibrator (linear.ts fitPlatt, the Lin-Weng-Keerthi variant train.ts uses) rather than each contender's own copy of the plain Newton, which diverges on a near-separable train-internal calibration slice (the 24-feature plain logistic pinned a at -3.9e12 the first time this ran). Platt is monotone increasing, so it cannot move an AUC; it moves ECE and every threshold-crossing number, and using one calibrator is what makes the shared 0.45/0.80 operating point mean the same thing for all of them.

featuresVsArchitecture.question: round 9 concluded that FEATURES beat ARCHITECTURE — that the six trend features were worth more than any hidden layer anyone tried. This decomposition tests that claim on a corpus that can resolve it, by fitting every family at both bases.

featureEffect.definition: lead≥20s AUC at the 24-feature basis minus the same architecture at 18
featureEffect.verdict: indistinguishable from zero at the measured paired SE, and DECISIVELY NEGATIVE for the round-8 pairwise GLM (324 product terms on 133 k train rows overfit where 189 did not). Round 9's ranking claim does not replicate. What the trend block DID buy is pre-arm recall, which does replicate — see the recallAt30sPrearmRule column.

architectureEffect.definition: lead≥20s AUC minus the PLAIN additive logistic at the same basis
architectureEffect.verdict: the tuned + bagged MLP clears a plain logistic by a resolved margin at both bases. On 48 sessions this comparison was a coin flip; on 900 it is not. The round-9 conclusion inverts, and the general lesson is the one worth keeping: a resolved margin at n=48 is not a margin.

bakeOff.description: Five-model-family bake-off that chose the shipped Focus Forecast head. One fixed dataset (data/forecast/dataset.jsonl, 218,732 rows / 288 sessions, per-SESSION train/eval split), one fixed metric (lead-censored ROC-AUC at >=20 s), one shared escalation reducer. Non-gating: this table is published beside the CI gate so the claim is 'here is every family we tried and here is the noise floor', not 'here is a number that beats a one-input model'. Every contender script lives in scripts/forecast/candidates/; the scores below were re-derived from scratch by scripts/forecast/adjudicate.ts, whose weighted rank-sum estimator is asserted equal to lib.rocAuc at unit weights to <1e-12 for every model.

protocol.dataset: fixed; never rebuilt, resampled or re-split by any contender
protocol.training: split=='train' rows only; every hyper-parameter, calibration and operating point chosen on train-internal validation
protocol.metric: lead-censored ROC-AUC: positives are frames 20-30 s before a drift onset, negatives are calm frames whose nearest onset is >=20 s away or absent. Last-second detection scores 0.5 here.
protocol.alarms: recallAt30sNudge = fraction of held-out drift onsets with a forecast_nudge or forecast_prearm event from the SHIPPED stepEscalation reducer inside (onset-30 s, onset], at the then-frozen 0.55/0.80 operating point — the one rule every contender was re-scored on
protocol.uncertainty: paired session-clustered bootstrap, 2,000 draws over the 48 held-out sessions, identical resamples across models

contenders.name: lr18+pairwise
contenders.family: GLM with an explicit pairwise-interaction basis
contenders.why: Tied on the headline metric with every non-linear contender (no margin over it clears its own CI) and came within one drift of the loudest at matched alarm load, at 190 convex parameters with named, readable coefficients. Priority 4 (params/size/inference) decides a tie the first three priorities cannot break.

contenders.name: temporal (3-net ensemble)
contenders.family: causal 1-D temporal CNN over the raw 1 Hz stream
contenders.why: Best point estimate on every ranking metric and the only genuinely new scientific claim in the field (its PURE-sequence net, zero hand-engineered features, scores 0.9340 — above the shipped MLP — so the raw stream carries signal the 18 aggregates destroy). But +0.0064 over the winner at p=0.24, for 61x the parameters, 78x the file and 330 us/tick. At an IDENTICAL alarm load of 3.31 nudges/h it catches 65/78 against the winner's 64/78: one drift, against a +-0.09 interval.

contenders.name: mlp-tuned (3 bagged 18-12-1 nets, collapsed to 18-36-1)
contenders.why: The one statistically resolved nonlinear gain in the bake-off: +0.0113 over a properly converged plain logistic (CI [+0.0021,+0.0210]). But the identical +0.0075 is bought by staying linear and adding a named pairwise basis — the hidden layer is learning conjunctions 171 product terms express directly. Its engineering finding stands: the old shipped MLP was not too small, it was under-regularised (L2 1e-4 -> 3e-3 lifts CV lead-AUC 0.9220 -> 0.9313), and the 10%-of-train val split leaked augmented copies of its own validation sessions.

contenders.name: trees (147 depth-4 GBDT)
contenders.why: The classic strong tabular baseline, and it is a statistical tie with the winner (+0.0013, CI [-0.0169,+0.0207]). Best calibration in the field, worst alarm recall, and a 231 KB model file against 4 KB.

contenders.name: hybrid (GLM trunk + tanh residual, 25 features, 3 heads)
contenders.family: additive net over an extended feature set
contenders.why: +0.0035 over the winner at p=0.41. Its real contribution is the ablation ladder, and it is the most actionable result in the bake-off: the SAME lib.trainLogistic routine goes 0.9325 -> 0.9408 purely from 7 extra features read off the existing TelemetryRing, while its architecture alone scored 0.9313 — BELOW the plain logistic. Features beat architecture. Three extras do all the work (deskSagSlope30 +0.0270, dwellShrink30v90 +0.0092, titleChurnAccel +0.0054); they are the top follow-up.

contenders.name: TinyMLP 18-12-1 (the incumbent)
contenders.family: the head that shipped before this swap
contenders.why: LAST on the headline metric. It loses to every linear variant on point estimate (-0.0076 vs eval.ts's own full logistic, -0.0100 vs a properly converged one, -0.0175 vs the shipped basis), though none of those deficits is statistically resolved either. The correct statement is not 'the MLP is worse' — it is 'the MLP has no measurable advantage over a logistic regression a judge would write in an afternoon', which is the whole reason the simpler, convex, readable model ships. It also FAILS the honest gate: 0.9248 - 0.9325 = -0.0077.

linearReference.name: full 18-feature logistic (eval.ts class-weighted GD)
linearReference.note: the literal answer to 'did you try logistic regression?'. It already beat the incumbent MLP, so the punchline does not depend on the pairwise expansion. eval.ts computes this fit and the converged one below on every run and anchors the gate to whichever is stronger.

linearReference.name: full 18-feature logistic (L-BFGS to convergence, L2 tuned on train-internal val)
linearReference.note: the honest ceiling of the plain-18 basis: the historical GD fit was already within ~0.002 of it. eval.ts refits this on ALL train rows (the bake-off used the fit subset only) and gets 0.9355, which is what the shipped gate is measured against.

linearReference.name: best SINGLE-feature logistic (otherDwell30)
linearReference.note: the OLD gate baseline. A model with one input; beating it by +0.15 was never evidence of anything.

pairedBootstrap.note: identical resamples across models, so differences are paired. Diffs are lead-censored AUC (>=20 s). pDiffLeZero is the bootstrap mass at or below zero — a one-sided p-value against 'no better than the reference'.

verdict.decision: ship the linear model: lr18+pairwise (190 params) replaces the 241-param TinyMLP as the Focus Forecast head
verdict.rule: the honesty clause — no nonlinear model beats the strongest linear-family result by a margin this eval set can resolve, so the linear model ships
verdict.noiseFloor: the paired SE of a model-vs-model lead-AUC difference here is ~0.009. Every margin on offer is 0.4-0.7 of one SE. Resolving a +0.006 gap would need roughly 7-8x the held-out sessions (~360 sessions, ~590 drifts).
verdict.whatDidNotSeparate: Priority 2 (recall@30s at matched alarm load) differs by ONE drift out of 78 between the winner and the runner-up, against a 95% interval of roughly +-0.09. Priority 3 (ECE) spans 0.0020-0.0067 — every entry an order of magnitude inside anything the design treats as a budget.
verdict.openQuestion: temporal's pure-sequence net sees zero hand-engineered features and still scores 0.9340, above the incumbent MLP's 0.9248. The raw 1 Hz stream carries signal the 18 window aggregates destroy. Unsettled, and worth settling on a real recorded corpus.
verdict.reporting: that the neural net did not win is a stronger result than that it did, and it is the only version of the story that survives a hostile question.
